confirmed: Source.version is correct: arXiv:2605.13776v1 [cs.HC], 13 May 2026, 32 pages, with the stated title/authors and Manuscript submitted to ACM footer (PDF p. 1; PDF page count). The entire markdown, through the final reference on p. 32, was read; there are no appended study materials in this file.

One within-person lab study qualifies as a randomized people study: each participant completed different tasks with and without GitHub Copilot; Fig. 2 explicitly states that condition and task-type order was randomized, and Sec. 4.1 describes counterbalancing and in-person sessions (PDF pp. 5-6, Sec. 4.1 and Fig. 2). Retain design_class = lab_rct, context_class = none, and criterion 1 = met.

There were 23 recruited students and 20 analyzed people after excluding P8 for discontinuation and P1/P2 for corrupted recordings; the same 20 people contributed to both conditions, and no explicit assignment-stage sample count is supplied (PDF p. 6, Sec. 4.2; p. 7, Table 1). Retain n_randomized = null and n_analyzed = 20; fewer than 50 people were analyzed.

The analyzed dataset comprises 80 programming-task outputs, with 40 task instances per condition, not 80 people or 40 independent people per arm (PDF p. 10, Secs. 5.3.1 and 6; p. 28, Sec. 11, Sample Size). The isolated p. 6 statement of 40 Algorithmic and 40 System Design tasks in each condition conflicts with these explicit totals and should not be used to inflate the sample.

Each person completed four Python tasks, one Algorithmic and one System Design task per condition, drawn from task sets A1-A4 and B1-B4 (PDF p. 6, Sec. 4.3). The task baseline was 15 minutes with extensions allowed (p. 7, Sec. 4.4), and mean total time per participant was 63.49 minutes (p. 11, Sec. 6).

GitHub Copilot was provided through its VS Code extension; unassisted sessions excluded external resources, and assisted sessions excluded resources other than Copilot (PDF pp. 5-6, Sec. 4.1). Prompting, chat-code adoption, and editing with autocompletion are documented (p. 9, Table 2); no underlying generative-model version is stated.

Output-based diversity and expert-rated correctness support criterion 3 = met; the 20-person analyzed sample supports criterion 2 = not_met and core = no under the codebook threshold (PDF pp. 6-7, Sec. 4.2 and Table 1; p. 10, Secs. 5.3.1-5.3.2). This is neither AI-only output comparison nor a synthesis.

S1-O1 retained counts are transcribed exactly: Algorithmic 16 Unassisted / 19 LLM-assisted solutions, yielding 120 / 171 pairs; System Design 11 / 14 solutions, yielding 55 / 91 pairs (PDF p. 10, Sec. 5.3.2). These are output and pair counts. The source leaves an unresolved inconsistency: its Unassisted retained counts total 27 (checker sum of 16 + 11), whereas Sec. 7.1 explicitly reports 29 correct-or-partially-correct Unassisted solutions (p. 13; see also p. 12, Table 4); no additional exclusion explanation is given.

S1-O1 Algorithmic statistics match exactly: LLM-assisted mean = 0.532, SD = 0.228; Unassisted mean = 0.492, SD = 0.239; U = 7880.0, p = 0.0008; permutation difference = -0.040, p = 0.161 (PDF p. 13, Sec. 7.2.1). Higher similarity means lower diversity; the permutation result is not significant.

S1-O1 System Design statistics match exactly: LLM-assisted mean = 0.505, SD = 0.237; Unassisted mean = 0.413, SD = 0.185; U = 1916.0, p = 0.018; permutation difference = -0.093, p = 0.016 (PDF pp. 13-14, Sec. 7.2.1).

S1-O2 reported counts match the source: 18 unique ideas per condition in the narrative; Algorithmic Unassisted 9 versus LLM-assisted 6, and System Design 11 versus 13 in Table 6; chi-square comparisons are described as nonsignificant without printed test statistics or p-values (PDF p. 16, Sec. 7.2.4 and Table 6).

S1-O3 is correctly recorded as 80 output units assessed by two expert raters: Correct / Partially Correct / Incorrect counts are Unassisted 18 / 11 / 11 and LLM-assisted 32 / 1 / 7; chi-square = 13.14, p < 0.01 (PDF p. 10, Sec. 5.3.1; p. 12, Table 4 and Sec. 7.1).

The one-line finding accurately reproduces 20 analyzed people, 32 versus 18 fully correct outputs out of 40 per condition, both task-type similarity results, and the narrative total of 18 unique ideas per condition; only its locator for that last total needs correction (PDF pp. 6-7, Sec. 4.2 and Table 1; p. 12, Table 4; pp. 13-14, Sec. 7.2.1; p. 16, Sec. 7.2.4).

The supplementary behavioral codebook is mentioned and contains 51 final codes; it is not appended to the 32-page PDF, and no access URL is given (PDF p. 8, Sec. 5.2; pp. 28-32 end with references). No synthesis study count, pooled effect, interval, or standardizer applies to this original experiment (pp. 5-10, Secs. 4-6).
summary: The paper contains a randomized within-person lab study with 20 analyzed students, so it belongs in the randomized-study pipeline but remains below the 50-person threshold. The reported results and source version are supported; corrections concern the education tally, omitted outcomes, missing methods/statistic metadata, and one finding locator.
